name: Donatus of Fiesole
bio: Donatus of Fiesole (died c. 876) was an Irish-born scholar who became bishop of Fiesole in Tuscany, in the ninth century. He is said to have travelled to Italy from Ireland and to have been made bishop around 829; he is remembered as one of the Irish churchmen active on the Continent in the Carolingian age.

The twelve Latin verses given here, in praise of Ireland under its old name Scottia, are traditionally attributed to him. They are printed complete from Stephen Gaselee's Oxford Book of Medieval Latin Verse (1928).

poems.title: Finibus occiduis describitur optima tellus
poems.author: Donatus of Fiesole
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Medieval Latin Verse (1928)
poems.text:
Finibus occiduis describitur optima tellus
nomine et antiquis Scottia scripta libris.
dives opum, argenti, gemmarum, vestis et auri,
commoda corporibus, aere, putre solo.
melle fluit pulchris et lacte Scottia campis,
vestibus atque armis, frugibus, arte, viris.
ursorum rabies nulla est ibi, saeva leonum
semina nec umquam Scottica terra tulit.
nulla venena nocent nec serpens serpit in herba
nec conquesta canit garrula rana lacu.
in qua Scottorum gentes habitare merentur,
inclita gens hominum milite, pace, fide.
